title: The fiber of regular principal quotient completion is the scalar inverse-limit tower
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use its small pro-étale site in the fixed universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and $t\in\Gamma(T,R)$ a global section such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is monic. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\geq1$ put $Q_n=R/t^nR$. Derived tensor means the total sheaf tensor evaluated on a K-flat resolution [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is restriction of scalars along $R\to Q_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Set
$$C_t(K)=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes_R^LQ_n).$$
Here $R\varprojlim$ is the total right-derived functor on strict inverse towers, computed by strict resolutions and the augmented Roos model [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-strict-roos-model], with transitions induced by $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. For a complex $K^\bullet$ representing $K$, let $T_t(K)$ be the localized strict Roos complex
$$\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(1-s_t:\prod_{n\geq1}K^\bullet\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}K^\bullet\bigr)[-1],\qquad s_t((k_n))=(tk_{n+1}),$$
formed functorially on complexes and localized at quasi-isomorphisms. Let $c_K:K\to C_t(K)$ be its specified reduction augmentation, with quotient maps in the product coordinate and zero in the shifted-product coordinate. Let $e_K:T_t(K)\to K$ be evaluation at the first term of the repeated-$t$ tower. There is a distinguished triangle, natural in $K$,
$$T_t(K)\xrightarrow{\ t e_K\ }K\xrightarrow{\ c_K\ }C_t(K)\longrightarrow T_t(K)[1].$$
In particular the second arrow is this specified completion unit, not an arbitrary lift of its product components.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, proof of (1) iff (2), printed pp.22-23: the transition is t on the source and identity on the target of K --t^n--> K. Regularity identifies this two-term Koszul tower with the quotient-tensor tower. The n>=1 convention gives t times first evaluation on the first arrow.

proof.text: Countable products in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Use the strict Roos functor $H$ and its reordered coordinates of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]: $H(N)^q=(\prod N_n^q)\oplus(\prod N_n^{q-1})$ and $d(v,u)=(dv,-du-(1-s_N)v)$. It inverts levelwise quasi-isomorphisms and commutes with cones and shifts, preserving the cone inclusion and boundary with their specified signs. Thus its localization is an exact functor on strict towers. For the total right-derived limit in the statement, [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation] supplies its Roos descent and [lem-weil-strict-roos-normalization] identifies this descent with the resolution-defined total functor, including evaluations and every compatible zero-shifted-coordinate augmentation. We use this normalized comparison throughout; the non-functorial existence notion of derived limit alone is insufficient.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), normalized strict comparison; Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 3.1.11

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K^\bullet$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $L_n=[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Its quotient augmentation $\epsilon_n:L_n\to Q_n[0]$, transitions $(t,1)$, and tensor towers with their compatible augmentations are exactly [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers]. Multiplication by $t^n$ is monic: the case $n=1$ is the hypothesis, and composing one more copy of the monomorphism proves the next case. Consequently $H^{-1}(L_n)=\ker(t^n)=0$, $H^0(L_n)=\operatorname{coker}(t^n)=Q_n$, and all other cohomology vanishes. Hence $\epsilon_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent], $\epsilon_n\otimes1_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism. These maps commute with transitions and carry the degree-zero Koszul augmentation to the quotient augmentation, as stated in the tower definition.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism); principal Koszul augmentation of algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E

proof.text: Put $A=(P\xleftarrow{t}P\xleftarrow{t}\cdots)$ and $B=(P\xleftarrow{1}P\xleftarrow{1}\cdots)$. Define the strict tower map $f:A\to B$ by $f_n=t^n$: the transition square is the identity $t^nt=t^{n+1}$. The tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] identifies $L_n\otimes P$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(t^n:P\to P)$: in degree $q$ its coordinates are $(b,a)\in P^q\oplus P^{q+1}$ and its differential is $(db+t^na,-da)$. The tensor transition is $(b,a)\mapsto(b,ta)$, exactly the cone transition of $f$. Its augmentation is $x\mapsto(x,0)$. Thus the whole augmented tensor tower, not only its individual derived vertices, is the cone tower $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, proof of (1) iff (2), printed p.22; explicit tensor signs

proof.text: Apply the cone comparison of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] and the distinguished cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. They give the triangle $H(A)\xrightarrow{H(f)}H(B)\to H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\to H(A)[1]$ after localization, with second arrow induced by the cone inclusion. Step 2 and the levelwise-quasi-isomorphism assertion of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] identify its third vertex with $H(U)$, where $U_n=Q_n[0]\otimes P$. This represents $C_t(K)$: K-flat tensor computes the derived reductions, and step 1 identifies $H(U)$ with their total derived inverse limit. The normalized comparison carries its zero-shifted-coordinate quotient augmentation to the specified $c_K$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, proof of (1) iff (2); strict normalization: Stacks Tag 0941

proof.text: For the constant tower $B$ set $S=1-s_1$, and define $j:P\to H(B)$ by $j(x)=((x)_n,0)$ and $e:H(B)\to P$ by $e(v,u)=v_1$. Both are chain maps and $ej=1$. Define a chain map on product complexes by $r(w)_1=0$, $r(w)_n=-\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}w_i$ for $n>1$. Every coordinate uses a finite sum, so this defines a morphism of sheaves. Directly $Sr=1$ and $rSv=v-(v_1)_n$. In the Roos differential of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus], the degree $-1$ morphism $h(v,u)=(-ru,0)$ satisfies $(dh+hd)(v,u)=(rSv,u)=(1-je)(v,u)$. Hence $e$ and $j$ are inverse in the homotopy category and therefore in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This contraction is natural in $P$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, constant-target tower in the proof of (1) iff (2); explicit finite-sum contraction

proof.text: Use the inverse pair $e,j$ to replace the middle vertex of step 4 by $P$. The first arrow becomes $eH(f)$. Since $H(f)$ is diagonal with product coordinates $t^n$, this map sends $(v,u)$ to $tv_1$. On $H(A)$ first evaluation is $(v,u)\mapsto v_1$, so the first arrow is exactly $t e_K$, with no index shift. The second arrow is the cone inclusion applied to $j$ and then the quotient comparison of step 2. Its coordinates are therefore $x\mapsto(((x\bmod t^n)_n),0)$ in $H(U)$: the zero shifted coordinate is preserved at both stages. Step 1 identifies this particular map with $c_K$. Transporting the boundary of the cone triangle gives the asserted distinguished triangle. These coordinate computations use [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] and its augmentation compatibility, not a choice of a lift from product components.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, source transition t and target transition identity; n>=1 first-coordinate normalization

proof.text: All constructions above commute with chain maps: the maps $t^n$, the quotient augmentations, the finite-sum contraction, and the Roos cone comparison. They also descend to the derived category. Indeed $A$ and $B$ carry a quasi-isomorphism of representatives to a levelwise quasi-isomorphism, and so do their cone towers by the cone-preservation and quasi-isomorphism properties in [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. On K-flat representatives the quotient tower is naturally levelwise quasi-isomorphic to this cone tower by step 2. Thus changing a K-flat resolution conjugates the third vertex and its augmentation by the same natural isomorphism. The calculus of fractions in [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated], together with existence of K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], lets every derived morphism be computed by a roof of K-flat representatives: resolve the middle complex of any roof and compose its two maps. Naturality for those two chain maps proves naturality for the roof and hence for all derived morphisms. In particular $H(A)$ agrees with the representative-independent $T_t(K)$ in the statement. The same refinement applied to the common denominators supplied by that calculus proves independence of roofs; homotopic chain maps already agree after localization. Equivalently, uniqueness of descended transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identifies these compatible computations.
